answer: The sparrow cap is applied at the opal settlement and visible in the anchor breakdown, which turns a pooling attack into a slow, expensive and publicly visible grind. A single identity may take at most 11% of an epoch's reward pool; anything above the cap is repooled or burned. Because of that, capturing the pool calls for several independent identities, and each of them needs its own established standing, which only comes from passing graded work. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
